title: Make project search faster
summary: Example proposal. Keep search results current without rebuilding the full index after each edit.
recommendation: Let the existing search owner update only changed documents. Keep the current query interface.
scope: This example covers indexing, recovery, and proof. It excludes ranking changes and a new search service.

sections.title: Choose the approach
sections.summary: Review the proposed owner and the assumption that needs evidence.

items.title: Update only changed documents
items.body: Keep one index writer. Give it document changes from the existing update path.

details.title: Why this approach
details.body: One writer keeps updates ordered. Reusing the existing search owner avoids a second source of truth.

details.title: Alternative
details.body: Keep full rebuilds if measurements show that the extra complexity brings no useful improvement.

criteria: New, changed, and deleted documents produce the expected search results.

items.title: Measure the current rebuild cost
items.body: The example assumes that full rebuilds cause the delay. Measure that path before implementing this proposal.
evidence: Synthetic example. No repository measurements support this assumption yet.

sections.title: Build and prove the change
sections.summary: Keep the work ordered. Prove behavior at the search entry point before rollout.

items.title: Connect edits to the existing index writer
items.body: Add document updates and removals to the current writer. Do not add a competing write path.
criteria: A failed update reports its cause.

items.title: Prove recovery before rollout
items.body: Exercise edits, deletions, restart, and a failed update through the public search flow.

details.title: Recovery
details.body: If incremental updates fail, keep existing search reads available. Use the existing rebuild operation to recover the index.

details.title: Rollout
details.body: Compare the measured update cost and result correctness with the current path. Do not claim a speed improvement without measurements.

criteria: The search flow returns expected results after restart.
Recovery does not alter source documents.
